post.summary: Fork a context (copy manifest into a fresh target)
post.description: Copies the source context's manifest and lifecycle metadata onto an **already-created** target context in the same project, so the target's query and curate gates pass. It does not create the target — create it first with `POST /contexts`. The target's index stays empty until curated. The source must have been optimized (`last_optimized_at` set) and must not be optimizing.

get.description: The context's pinned manifest document. A context with no pinned manifest returns `{}` — the runtime fills defaults. Writes go through the `manifest` field on `PUT /contexts/{slug}`.

post.description: "Curate the staged sources under the active manifest. **Required before querying** — there is no auto-curate. Body is optional. Set `force: true` to do a full rebuild (use after editing the manifest); the default is an incremental curate. Search contexts only — a work context builds via `work`/`groom` instead."

get.description: "The full ledger: per-source hashes, edges, corpus groups, chunk-id lineage, version pin, reclaim intents, pointers, and glossary. This pays an O(corpus) chunk-id-lineage read — use `GET /contexts/{slug}/curate/version/pin` on the per-turn path."

post.summary: Drop named sources from the index + ledger

post.description: Tunes the manifest from real query traffic and chains a forced re-curate. A body is required but every field in it is optional, so `{}` is valid — and a no-op when no `candidate_queries` are supplied. The context must have been curated, and only one optimize runs at a time.

post.summary: Run the Design-flow explore agent (propose a manifest)
post.description: Inspects the uploaded source and proposes manifest-template matches, returned in the task's `output` (see `ExploreOutput`). Persists nothing on the index — review the proposal, then apply it via the manifest update + a forced curate. Body is optional.

post.summary: Estimate the token + time cost of curating the in-progress manifest
post.description: Spins up the `profile` runtime to estimate the token + time cost of curating the sources under the in-progress manifest (sent in the request body), returned as the task's `output` (see `ProfileEstimateOutput`). Persists nothing; the console polls it for the Design-page cost box. Body is optional.

post.summary: Import source documents from a project connector
post.description: Pull source documents from a linked project connector (Box, ...) into the context. Supply either `folder` or `files`. Stages the source only — curate explicitly before querying.

post.summary: Upload a source file or archive
post.description: One file per request, max 2 GiB. Archives (`.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`) are expanded by the import runtime. Stages the source only — it does not index anything. Curate explicitly with `POST /contexts/{slug}/curate` before querying.

post.description:
"Send `ask` (the natural-language question) and, when starting a new session, a `scope` of 1–10 contexts. Continue an existing session with `session_id` or `previous_query_id`. Scoped search contexts must be curated (work contexts are queryable immediately), and a scope may not mix work and search contexts.

`stream` and `background` are mutually exclusive. With `background: true` the API returns `202` with an `in_progress` query and the client polls `GET /queries/{id}`. With `stream: true` the API emits an SSE stream whose `event:` names are the event `type` (`response.created`, `response.step`, `response.output_text.delta`, `response.turn_rollup`, `response.synthesis`, `response.trace`, and a terminal `response.completed` / `response.failed` / `response.cancelled`), followed by a final `query` event carrying the full query object. Read the answer from `output[].content[].text`."

200.description: The completed query turn (synchronous), or the SSE stream when `stream=true`

post.description: Idempotent — an already-terminal query is returned unchanged. On success the turn's `status` becomes `cancelled`.

get.summary: Fetch the recorded trace for a query turn
get.description: The per-turn debug trace (steps, tool calls, strategy, cost, rollup). Trace persistence is unconditional — every turn lands a trace blob — so this is available once the turn is terminal.

"Server-sent event stream of the turn's events as they land — the same `type`-named events POST /query emits with `stream: true`, but as a standalone, resumable subscription. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` to replay from where the stream dropped."

200.description: SSE event stream; each `event:` name is the event `type` and `data:` is its JSON payload.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Resume from this event seq; delivery is inclusive of the given id (re-sending the last event is harmless — clients merge steps idempotently by step_id).

Only entries with `available: true` are selectable (others are coming soon and rejected with `400`)."

Nexus202607Query200EventStreamResponse.description:
"Server-sent event stream. While the turn runs, each progress frame has an `id:` (the event's sequence number — send it back as the `Last-Event-ID` header to resume), an `event:` name equal to the QueryEvent `type` (e.g. `response.step`), and that QueryEvent as its JSON `data:`. When the turn finishes, a final frame named `event: query` is sent — no `id:`, with the full Query document as `data:`.
"

When the turn finishes, a final frame named `event: query` is sent — no `id:`, with the full Query document as `data:`.
"
